paragraphs: Nabors Industries, Ltd. (NYSE: NBR) was formed as a Bermuda exempted company on December 11, 2001. Unless the context requires otherwise, references in this annual report to "we," "us," "our," "the Company," or "Nabors" mean Nabors Industries Ltd., together with our subsidiaries. References in this annual report to "Nabors Delaware" mean Nabors Industries, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Nabors.

Nabors owns and operates one of the world's largest land-based drilling rig fleets and is a provider of offshore platform rigs in the United States and numerous international markets. Nabors also supplies performance software, tubular running services, managed pressure drilling services and innovative technologies for both its own rig fleet and those operated by third parties. In addition, Nabors manufactures advanced drilling equipment and provides drilling rig instrumentation. Also, Nabors has developed a portfolio of technologies designed to drive energy efficiency and emissions reductions for both itself and third-party customers. One key component of Nabors' strategy is to seamlessly integrate downhole hardware, surface equipment and software solutions into rig designs that drive industry-leading performance and increasing efficiencies. A second component is to leverage advanced drilling automation capabilities to set new standards for operational excellence and transform the industry.

With operations in over 20 countries, we are a global provider of drilling and drilling-related services for land-based and offshore oil and natural gas wells. As of December 31, 2025, Nabors' fleet of drilling rigs and drilling-related equipment included:
● 242 actively marketed rigs for land-based drilling operations in the United States and multiple international markets; and
● 27 actively marketed rigs for offshore platform drilling operations in the United States and various countries throughout the world.
The following table presents our average rigs working (a measure of activity and utilization over the year) for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023:
U.S. Drilling 69.9 75.1 86.3 International Drilling 88.4 83.7 77.6 Total 158.3 158.8 163.9

Average rigs working represents a measure of the number of equivalent rigs operating during a given period. For example, one rig operating 182.5 days during a 365-day period represents 0.5 average rigs working.
Our business consists of four reportable segments: U.S. Drilling, International Drilling, Drilling Solutions and Rig Technologies.

Additional information regarding the geographic markets in which we operate and our business segments can be found in Note 17—Segment Information in Part II, Item 8.—Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.

Nabors operates one of the largest land-based drilling rig fleets in the U.S. We continue to drive innovation and integration in the industry. We are active in the major hydrocarbon basins across the Lower 48 market and Alaska as well as offshore in the Gulf of America. Our marketed U.S. fleet as of December 31, 2025 consists of 121 land rigs and 13 offshore platform rigs.

Nabors has a long history of developing and deploying industry-leading breakthroughs, beginning with our first AC-powered land rig nearly 25 years ago. In 2025, we introduced our PACE®-X Ultra rig, an upgrade to our PACE®-X800 rig. The PACE®-X Ultra combines upgrades to the rig's most important specifications. We believe it is the Lower 48 drilling industry's most powerful rig. It is designed to enable operators to drill their longest, most challenging oil and gas wells.

In recent years we have developed and deployed a full suite of technology supporting Nabors and third-party rigs. Demonstrating Nabors technology leadership, we employ automation to improve safety, increase efficiencies and build agility for our customers. Also in 2025, Nabors deployed an upgraded version of its Rig Zone Robotics (RZR) rig floor automation module, on existing Nabors rigs. RZR fully automates tubular handling on the rig, removing rig crew from higher-risk manual operations. See "—Drilling Solutions" below for more information.

We operate in major international oil and gas markets, primarily in the Middle East and Latin America, most notably Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Argentina, Colombia and Mexico. Many of our rigs are designed to address the challenges of working in specific operating environments, such as desert climates, mountainous regions, and tropical zones.

headings: Share Capital and Corporate Structure Risks
Fluctuations in oil and natural gas prices could adversely affect drilling activity and our revenues, cash flows and profitability.
Our customers and thereby our business and profitability could be adversely affected by low oil prices or turmoil in the global economy.
We operate in a highly competitive industry with excess drilling capacity, which may adversely affect our results of operations.
We must renew customer contracts to remain competitive.
The nature of our operations presents inherent risks of loss, including weather-related risks, that could adversely affect our results of operations.
Our drilling contracts may in certain instances be renegotiated, suspended or terminated without an early termination payment.
The loss of one or a number of our large customers could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Significant changes or developments in U.S. or other national trade policies, including tariffs, and the reactions of other countries thereto, may have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.
We rely on third-party suppliers, manufacturers and service providers to secure equipment, components and parts used in rig operations, conversions, upgrades and construction.
Our contracts with state-owned energy companies may expose us to greater risks than we normally assume in contracts with non-governmental customers.
Control of oil and natural gas reserves by NOCs may affect the demand for our services and products and create additional risks in our operations.
Our operating expense includes fixed costs that may not decline in proportion to decreases in rig utilization and dayrates.

Failure to realize the anticipated benefits of acquisitions, divestitures, investments, joint ventures and other strategic transactions may adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial position.

Decisions by internet service, cloud host service and related providers to restrict or ban our ability to use their platforms could adversely affect our ability to promote and conduct our business and inform investors.
Failure to effectively and timely address the energy transition could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows and share price.
Our aspirations, goals and initiatives related to sustainability and emissions reduction, and our public statements and disclosures regarding them, expose us to risks.
We may record additional losses or impairment charges related to sold or idle drilling rigs and other assets.
Our financial and operating flexibility could be affected by our long-term debt and other financial commitments.
Volatility in prices of goods and services and interest rates could expose us to risks in managing our operating and capital costs.
Our ability to access capital markets could be limited.
A downgrade in our credit rating could negatively affect our cost of and ability to access capital markets or other financing sources.
Limitations on our ability to obtain, maintain, protect or enforce our intellectual property rights, including our trade secrets, could cause a loss in revenues and any competitive advantage we hold.
Technology disputes could negatively affect our operations or increase our costs.
Improvements in or new discoveries of alternative energy technologies could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
Our business is subject to cybersecurity risks.
paragraphs: In addition to the other information set forth elsewhere in this annual report, the following factors should be carefully considered when evaluating Nabors. The risks described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business operations.
The following is a summary of the principal risks included in this annual report that we believe could adversely affect our business, operations, and financial results.
● Fluctuations in oil and natural gas prices could adversely affect drilling activity and our revenues, cash flows and profitability.
● We operate in a highly competitive industry with excess drilling capacity, which may adversely affect our results of operations.
● The nature of our operations presents inherent risks of loss, including weather-related risks, that could adversely affect our results of operations.
● Our drilling contracts may in certain instances be renegotiated, suspended or terminated on short notice or without an early termination payment.

This section of this Form 10-K generally discusses fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024. Discussions of fiscal 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in "Part II, Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" of the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year December 31, 2024, as filed with the SEC on February 13, 2025, which is available on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov.

We are a leading provider of advanced technology for the energy industry. With operations in over 20 countries, Nabors has established a global network of people, technology and equipment to deploy solutions that deliver safe, efficient and sustainable energy production. By leveraging its core competencies, particularly in drilling, engineering, automation, data science and manufacturing, Nabors aims to innovate the future of energy and enable the transition to a lower carbon world.

The demand for our services and products is a function of the level of spending by oil and gas companies for exploration, development and production activities. The level of exploration, development and production activities is to a large extent tied to the prices of oil and natural gas, which can fluctuate significantly, are highly volatile and tend to be highly sensitive to factors including supply and demand cycles and geopolitical uncertainties particularly those impacting large hydrocarbon-producing countries. Certain oil and gas companies may also intentionally limit their capital spending as they focus on generating returns to shareholders as opposed to maximizing hydrocarbon production. Additionally, in recent years significant consolidation among oil and gas companies has taken place, especially in the United States. In some cases, these transactions may have an impact on overall rig demand, as the acquiring company may apply criteria that results in a different level of demand for drilling rigs than the previous two companies would have had on a stand-alone basis.

Since late 2022 and continuing through the fourth quarter of 2025, global energy commodity markets have experienced sustained volatility driven by evolving geopolitical dynamics, and more recently, domestic policy changes. In the U.S., operators generally reacted to these market conditions with caution by reducing their drilling activity – particularly in the natural gas basins. This trend appears to be shifting with the expectation for higher natural gas demand in the future. Meanwhile, a number of operators in oil-driven basins, especially the Permian Basin, have reduced drilling activity as they have realized efficiency gains and achieved their production goals.
Despite the reduction in overall rig count in the United States, pricing discipline for drilling rigs in this market remained intact, generally supporting rig dayrates and daily rig margins.

Oil prices have been impacted by recent production actions announced by certain large international oil producers. Natural gas prices, particularly in the United States, have generally increased, in part as demand increased as LNG export facilities ramped throughput.
U.S. oil and gas production has proved resilient in the face of reduced drilling activity aided by efficiency gains.

Internationally, we generally see an expansion of production capacity as well as the widespread development of unconventional resources driving an expected increase in oilfield activity broadly across those markets. In Saudi Arabia specifically, the operating rig fleet has begun to rebound following the activity suspensions in 2024 of a large number of rigs.

On March 11, 2025, Nabors completed its merger with Parker Drilling Company ("Parker") resulting in Parker becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of Nabors. Parker provides drilling services across global energy markets. Total consideration for the acquisition included cash consideration of $0.6 million and the issuance of 4.8 million shares of our common stock, which based on the closing price of our common stock of $37.50 on March 11, 2025, valued the purchase price consideration of the transaction at approximately $180.6 million.

On August 20, 2025, Nabors entered into a definitive agreement to sell Quail Tools to Superior Energy Services, Inc. Quail Tools was part of Nabors' acquisition of Parker. Net consideration for the sale totals $625.0 million inclusive of a net working capital adjustment. Consideration comprised of cash of $375.0 million and a seller note of $250.0 million. On October 9, 2025, Nabors received prepayment in full of the $250.0 million seller note, including accrued and unpaid interest.

On November 10, 2025, Nabors issued $700.0 million in aggregate principal amount of 7.625% senior priority guaranteed notes, which are fully and unconditionally guaranteed by Nabors and certain of Nabors' indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries. Interest on the notes is payable on May 15 and November 15 of each year. The notes have a maturity date of November 15, 2032. Nabors used the net proceeds to redeem all of its 7.375% senior priority guaranteed notes due May 2027.

Operating revenues in 2025 totaled $3.2 billion, representing an increase of $254.6 million, or 9%, from 2024. For a more detailed description of operating results see Segment Results of Operations, below.

Net income attributable to Nabors totaled $286.6 million for 2025 ($17.39 per diluted share) compared to a net loss attributable to Nabors of $176.1 million ($22.37 per diluted share) in 2024, or a $462.7 million increase in net income. Adjusted operating income (loss) across our operating segments, increased by $54.3 million, or 13%. $113.7 million of the increase is due to the gain on bargain purchase related to the Parker acquisition and $414.0 million was due to the gain on the disposition of Quail Tools. These gains were partially offset by $26.5 million of asset impairments related to assets held in Russia, $24.6 million related to severance and reorganization costs and $19.9 million of transaction related costs. See Segment Results of Operations and Other Financial Information below for additional discussion.

headings: 平均鑽井 rigs 運作數
paragraphs: Nabors Industries, Ltd. (NYSE: NBR) 於 2001 年 12 月 11 日成立為一間百慕達豁免公司。除非上下文另有明確要求，否則本年度報告中提及 "we," "us," "our," "the Company," 或 "Nabors" 均指 Nabors Industries Ltd.，包含其所有子公司。本年度報告中提及 "Nabors Delaware" 均指 Nabors Industries, Inc.，為 Nabors 的 wholly owned subsidiary。

Nabors 擁有並營運全球最大的陸上鑽井 rigs 之一，同時為美國及多個國際市場的 offshore platform rigs 提供服務。Nabors 還提供性能軟體、管柱下放服務、_managed pressure drilling 服務及創新技術，用於其自有 rigs 以及由第三方營運的 rigs。此外，Nabors 還製造先進鑽井設備並提供鑽井 rigs 的儀器設備。Nabors 還開發了一套技術組合，用以提升自身及第三方客戶的能源效率與減排效益。Nabors 策略的一個關鍵零組件是將 downhole 硬體、表面設備與軟體解決方案無縫整合至 rigs 設計中，以實現行業領先的表現與持續提升的效率。另一個關鍵零組件是利用先進鑽井自動化能力，設立新的運營卓越標準並改變產業。
我們在超過 20 個國家擁有營運據點，為陸上及 offshore 的石油與天然氣井提供鑽井及相關服務。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Nabors 的鑽井 rigs 與相關設備包含：
● 242 臺 actively marketed rigs 用於美國及多個國際市場的陸上鑽井作業；以及
● 27 臺 actively marketed rigs 用於美國及世界各地各國的 offshore platform 鑽井作業。
下表呈現我們在 2025 年 12 月 31 日結止年度、2024 年 12 月 31 日結止年度及 2023 年 12 月 31 日結止年度的平均 rigs 工作數（為衡量年度內活動與使用率的指標）：
U.S. Drilling 69.9 75.1 86.3 International Drilling 88.4 83.7 77.6 Total 158.3 158.8 163.9
平均 rigs 工作數為衡量特定期間內等效 rigs 運作數量的指標。例如，一臺 rigs 在 365 天期間運作 182.5 天，則代表 0.5 平均 rigs 工作數。
本公司業務包含四個應報告分部：美國鑽井、國際鑽井、鑽井解決方案與鑽井技術。
有關本公司營運之地理市場及業務分部之額外資訊，請參閱第二部分，第 8 項—財務報表及補充資料中的附註 17—分部資訊。
Nabors 在美國擁有其中一支規模最大的陸上鑽井 rigs 船隊。本公司持續推動產業創新與整合。本公司在美國下 48 州及阿拉斯加的主要氫碳化合物盆地，以及美國墨西哥灣 offshore 市場均有積極參與。本公司截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止的美國 marketed 船隊，包含 121 臺陸上 rigs 與 13 臺 offshore 平台 rigs。

Nabors 有長久的歷史，持續開發與部署產業領先的突破性技術，從我們近 25 年前推出的首部 AC 電動陸上 rigs 開始。2025 年，本公司推出 PACE®-X Ultra rigs，為 PACE®-X800 rigs 的升級版。PACE®-X Ultra 結合了 rigs 最重要規格的升級。本公司認為這是美國下 48 州鑽井產業最強大的 rigs。其設計目的是讓操作者能鑽探他們最長、最具挑戰性的石油與天然氣井。

近年來，本公司已開發並部署一套完整的技術，支援 Nabors 及第三方 rigs。展現 Nabors 的技術領導地位，本公司運用自動化技術以提升安全性、增加效率並為客戶建立靈活性。2025 年，Nabors 部署了其 Rig Zone Robotics (RZR) rigs 操作平台自動化模組的升級版，應用於現有 Nabors rigs。RZR 完全自動化處理 rigs 上的管柱操作，將 rigs 人員從高風險的手動作業中移除。有關更多資訊，請參閱下方「—鑽井解決方案」部分。
本公司營運於主要國際石油與天然氣市場，主要位於中東與拉丁美洲，特別是沙特阿拉伯、科威特、阿根廷、哥倫比亞與墨西哥。許多本公司 rigs 是為應對特定作業環境的挑戰而設計，例如沙漠氣候、山區與熱帶地區。

本 10-K 表單之此節通常討論財務年度 2025 及財務年度 2024 之項目，以及財務年度 2025 與財務年度 2024 之間的年對年比較。未包含於本 10-K 表單中之財務年度 2023 項目及財務年度 2024 與財務年度 2023 之間之年對年比較，可於本公司於 2025 年 2 月 13 日向 SEC 提交之財務年度 2024 年 12 月 31 日之年度報告，第二部分，第 7 項—管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析中找到。
本公司為能源產業提供先進科技之領導供應商。本公司在全球超過 20 個國家設有營運據點，已建立全球人力、科技與設備網路，以部署解決方案，提供安全、高效且可持續的能源生產。透過運用其核心專長，特別是在鑽井、工程、自動化、資料科學與製造領域，本公司旨在創新能源的未來，並促進向低碳世界的過渡。
本公司服務與產品之需求，取決於油氣公司於探勘、開發與生產活動之支出水平。探勘、開發與生產活動之程度，在很大程度上與原油與天然氣價格相關，這些價格可能大幅波動，具有高度不穩定性，且對供需週期及地緣政治不確定性，特別是影響大型石化產品生產國家之因素，反應極為敏感。某些油氣公司也可能有意限制其資本支出，因其更著重於產生回報給股東，而非最大化石化產品之生產。
自 2022 年末以來，持續至 2025 年第四季，全球能源商品市場經歷了持續的波動，主因於不斷演變的地緣政治動態，以及近期國內政策變動。在美國，營運者通常對這些市場情況反應謹慎，減少其鑽井活動—特別是在天然氣盆地。此趨勢似乎正在轉變，因未來對天然氣需求預期增加。同時，一些在油氣驅動盆地，特別是在二號盆地的營運者，已減少鑽井活動，因其已實現效率提升並達成其生產目標。
儘管美國整體鑽井 rigs 數量減少，但此市場之鑽井 rigs 價格紀律仍維持完整，通常支撐鑽井 rigs 日租金與每日鑽井 rigs 毛利率。
原油價格已受到某些大型國際原油生產者近期生產行動之影響。天然氣價格，特別是在美國，已普遍上漲，部分原因為 LNG 出口設施提高輸送量，導致需求增加。
美國油氣生產在面對鑽井活動減少的情況下，已證明其韌性，受益於效率提升。
國際間，我們通常觀察到生產能力的擴張以及非常規資源的廣泛開發，驅動了油氣田活動在這些市場廣泛增加。特別是在沙特阿拉伯，營運鑽井 rigs 的數量已開始回升，這是因為 2024 年有大量 rigs 的活動暫停。

2025 年 3 月 11 日，Nabors 完成與 Parker Drilling Company（"Parker"）的合併，導致 Parker 成為 Nabors 的 wholly owned subsidiary。Parker 提供全球能源市場的鑽井服務。此次收購的總對價包含現金對價 0.6 百萬美元，以及發行 4.8 百萬股我們的普通股，根據 2025 年 3 月 11 日我們普通股的收盤價 37.50 美元，該交易的購買價格對價估值約為 180.6 百萬美元。

2025 年 8 月 20 日，Nabors 與 Superior Energy Services, Inc. 籤訂最終協議，出售 Quail Tools。Quail Tools 是 Nabors 收購 Parker 的一部分。此次出售的淨對價總計為 625.0 百萬美元，包含淨營運資金調整。對價包含現金 375.0 百萬美元，以及賣方貸款 250.0 百萬美元。2025 年 10 月 9 日，Nabors 收到賣方貸款 250.0 百萬美元的全額預付款，包含累計未付利息。

2025 年 11 月 10 日，Nabors 發行總本金金額為 700.0 百萬美元的 7.625% 高優先權擔保債券，該債券由 Nabors 及其部分間接 wholly-owned 子公司無條件及完全擔保。債券利息於每年 5 月 15 日及 11 月 15 日支付。債券的到期日為 2032 年 11 月 15 日。Nabors 使用淨資金贖回其所有 7.375% 高優先權擔保債券，到期日為 2027 年 5 月。
2025 年營運收入總計為 3.2 十億美元，較 2024 年增加 254.6 百萬美元，或 9%。如需更詳細的營運結果說明，請參閱下方的 Segment Results of Operations。

2025 年歸屬於 Nabors 的淨收入為 286.6 百萬美元（每股稀釋後 17.39 美元），較 2024 年歸屬於 Nabors 的淨虧損 176.1 百萬美元（每股稀釋後 22.37 美元）增加 462.7 百萬美元。我們營運分部的調整營運收入（損失）增加 54.3 百萬美元，或 13%。其中 113.7 百萬美元的增加係因 Parker 收購相關的 bargain purchase 優惠收益，414.0 百萬美元則因 Quail Tools 出售產生的收益。這些收益部分被 26.5 百萬美元的俄羅斯資產減損、24.6 百萬美元的遣散及重整費用，以及 19.9 百萬美元的交易相關費用所抵銷。有關更多討論，請參閱下方的 Segment Results of Operations 及 Other Financial Information。

headings: 原油與天然氣價格波動可能不利於鑽探活動及我們的營業收入、現金流與獲利能力。
我們的客戶及因此我們的業務與獲利能力可能因低油價或全球經濟動盪而受到不利影響。
我們所處的產業為高度競爭，且鑽井能力過度，這可能會對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
我們必須更新客戶合約以維持競爭力。
我們的營運性質會導致潛在的損失風險，包括天氣相關風險，這可能會對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
我們的鑽井合約在某些情況下可能被重新協議、暫停或終止，而無需提前終止補償金。
我們失去一個或數個大型客戶，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生重大不利影響。
美國或其他國家貿易政策的重大變動或發展，包括關稅，以及其他國家對此的反應，可能會對我們的業務及營運結果產生重大不利影響。
我們依賴第三方供應商、製造商及服務提供者，以取得用於鑽井作業、轉換、升級及建設的設備、零組件及零件。
我們與國營能源公司的合約可能使我們面臨較我們通常在非政府客戶合約中承擔的更高風險。
國營企業對石油與天然氣儲備的控制可能影響我們服務與產品的需求，並在我們營運中產生額外風險。
我們的營運費用包含固定成本，這些成本可能不會隨著鑽井 rigs 使用率與日費下降而同比例減少。
未能實現併購、出售、投資、合資企業及其他戰略交易預期的效益，可能對我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況產生不利影響。
網際網路服務、雲端主機服務及其他相關服務提供者決定限制或禁止我們使用其平台，可能對我們推廣及進行業務、向投資者傳達資訊的能力產生不利影響。
未能有效且及時應對能源轉型，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流與股價產生不利影響。
我們與永續性及排放量減少相關的願景、目標與計畫，以及我們公開聲明與披露的相關資訊，使我們面臨風險。
我們可能因出售或閒置的鑽井 rigs 及其他資產而記錄額外的虧損或減損費用。
我們的財務與營運彈性可能受到長期債務及其他財務承諾的影響。
商品與服務價格及利率的波動可能使我們面臨管理營運及資本成本的風險。
我們取得資本市場資金的能力可能受到限制。
我們的信用評級遭降級可能不利於我們的資金成本及取得資本市場或其它融資來源的能力。
我們取得、維持、保護或執行智慧財產權權利，包括我們的商業機密的能力受到限制，可能導致收入減少及我們所持有的任何競爭優勢喪失。
科技爭議可能不利於我們的營運或增加我們的成本。
替代能源科技的改善或新發現可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
我們的業務面臨網路安全風險。
paragraphs: 除本年度報告其他部分所載之資訊外，評估 Nabors 時應謹慎考慮下列因素。下列所描述之風險並非我們所面臨之唯一風險。尚有其他未為我們所知或目前認為不重要之風險，亦可能影響我們之業務運作。
下列為本年度報告中所包含之主要風險摘要，我們認為這些風險可能對我們之業務、運作及財務結果產生不利影響。
● 油價與天然氣價格之波動可能對鑽井活動及我們之營業收入、現金流及獲利能力產生不利影響。
● 我們所處之產業為高度競爭，且鑽井能力過度供給，這可能對我們之運作結果產生不利影響。
● 我們之業務性質存在導致損失之內在風險，包括天氣相關風險，這可能對我們之運作結果產生不利影響。
● 我們之鑽井合約在某些情況下可能在短時間內被重新協議、中止或終止，且不附有提前終止補償金。
